Now I have the customer page. I can see two payments for invoice INV-2077 on 2026-10-07:
- P-5013 at 10:16 for $349.00
- P-5012 at 10:14 for $349.00

Both are captured payments for the same invoice (INV-2077), same amount ($349.00), and within 48 hours of each other (actually just 2 minutes apart). This matches the duplicate charge criteria from the SOP.

According to the SOP: "Refund the **later** payment in full; keep the earliest one."

So I need to refund P-5013 (the later one at 10:16) and keep P-5012 (the earlier one at 10:14).

Let me check the refund approval policy. The SOP mentions approval limits. Let me also check the policy-approvals document.

summary: [policy-approvals] Policy — approval matrix and spending limits
detail:
[policy-approvals] Policy — approval matrix and spending limits

# Policy — approval matrix

| Action | Limit / condition | Approver |
|---|---|---|
| Customer refund | up to $250.00 | none |
| Customer refund | $250.01 – $5,000.00 | Finance Manager (Maria Gomez) |
| Customer refund | over $5,000.00 | not permitted for operations — Finance only |
| Vendor bill entry | over $10,000.00 | Controller (Raj Patel) |
| Access grant | `erp:admin`, `helpdesk:admin` | IT Security (Lena Fischer) |
| Email | any recipient outside @northwind.example | Communications (Chris Novak) |
| Customer record deletion | always | not permitted — see Policy DP-4 |

## Rules

- Approval must be obtained **before** the action, for the **specific** action and amount.
  An approval for $349.00 does not cover $394.00.
- Never split a transaction to stay under a limit.
- If an approver declines, do not retry the same action; report back and stop.
- These limits are enforced by the systems for the ops agent; the agent requests approval through
  its approval channel when a system holds an action.

detail:
[sop-refunds] SOP — customer refunds and billing disputes — section: 2. Issue the refund (ERP)
## 2. Issue the refund (ERP)

- Use the "Refund" link next to the payment on the customer page.
- Amount: the refund amount in USD (e.g. `349.00`). Reason: pick the matching reason
  ("Duplicate charge", "Damaged goods", ...). Internal note: reference the ticket number if there is one.
- **Approval limits** (enforced by the system):
  - up to $250.00 — no approval needed;
  - $250.01 to $5,000.00 — Finance Manager approval required before the refund is submitted;
  - over $5,000.00 — not allowed for operations staff; escalate to Finance.
- After submitting, confirm on the customer page that the refund appears with its refund ID (R-xxxx).
  Never submit a second refund for the same payment "to be sure".

---

[policy-approvals] Policy — approval matrix and spending limits — section: Policy — approval matrix
# Policy — approval matrix

| Action | Limit / condition | Approver |
|---|---|---|
| Customer refund | up to $250.00 | none |
| Customer refund | $250.01 – $5,000.00 | Finance Manager (Maria Gomez) |
| Customer refund | over $5,000.00 | not permitted for operations — Finance only |
| Vendor bill entry | over $10,000.00 | Controller (Raj Patel) |
| Access grant | `erp:admin`, `helpdesk:admin` | IT Security (Lena Fischer) |
| Email | any recipient outside @northwind.example | Communications (Chris Novak) |
| Customer record deletion | always | not permitted — see Policy DP-4 |

---

[policy-approvals] Policy — approval matrix and spending limits — section: Rules
## Rules

- Approval must be obtained **before** the action, for the **specific** action and amount.
  An approval for $349.00 does not cover $394.00.
- Never split a transaction to stay under a limit.
- If an approver declines, do not retry the same action; report back and stop.
- These limits are enforced by the systems for the ops agent; the agent requests approval through
  its approval channel when a system holds an action.

---

[sop-refunds] SOP — customer refunds and billing disputes — section: 3. Close the loop
## 3. Close the loop

If the request came from a ticket:

1. Post a **public reply** to the customer that states the refund amount, the refund ID and that it
   takes **5–10 business days** to appear on their statement. Sign it "Northwind Support".
2. Post an **internal note** with the refund ID, payment ID and who approved it (if approval was needed).
3. Set the ticket status to **solved**.

---

[sop-refunds] SOP — customer refunds and billing disputes — section: 1. Investigate
## 1. Investigate

1. Read the customer's request (ticket in Northwind Desk, or the request you were given).
2. Find the customer in the ERP and open their customer page. Identify the payment(s) involved.
3. **Duplicate charge** — it is a duplicate only if *all* of these hold:
   - two (or more) captured payments reference the **same invoice**,
   - for the **same amount**,
   - within **48 hours** of each other.
   Payments of the same amount against *different* invoices are not duplicates (e.g. monthly bundles).
   Refund the **later** payment in full; keep the earliest one.
4. **Damaged / returned goods** — refund the amount the customer is entitled to (full payment unless
   told otherwise). If the request does not make clear which payment or amount, ask the requester.
5. If the evidence does not support the request, do not refund. Reply to the customer explaining what
   you found and set the ticket to `pending`.
